name: Bad Taste Department
tagline: Taste is subjective. Yours has been entered into evidence.
summary: A citation in defense of questionable taste.
public: A named citation, your dedication and a choice of classic, chaos or terminal presentation.
private: Award a taste citation, then use the included debate prompt at your next gathering.
example: Defend the indefensible: explain why this choice belongs in a museum.

name: A Minute of Silence
tagline: For something that probably did not need commemorating.
summary: A solemn minute for a very small loss.
public: A dedication with a replayable sixty-second ceremony on its own public page.
private: Give a dedication and invite the recipient to observe an entirely optional minute of silence.
example: In memory of the coffee that went cold before the meeting ended.

name: The Sponsored Loading Bar
tagline: Progress has acquired a patron. It is still going nowhere.
public: A named sponsor credit on a five-second loading ceremony. No real service is delayed.
private: Give a five-second loading ceremony to someone who has been waiting impressively.
example: For patiently waiting for something that could have been an email.

name: The Last Word
public: Your short final statement and chosen alias on a shareable page. Other statements remain separate.
private: Give someone a beautifully formal last word, then take turns ending an imaginary debate.
example: I maintain that the snacks were the most important part of the meeting.

name: The Ordinary Museum
tagline: Everyday objects. An entirely unnecessary curatorial department.
summary: An exhibit label for an unremarkable object.
public: A text-only exhibit with object title, curator alias and caption. No photo upload in this edition.
private: Print an exhibit label, place it beside an ordinary object and conduct a tiny guided tour.
example: A faithful mug. Present at more meetings than most of the team.

name: A Gold-Plated Error
public: A fictional 404 dedication with a named patron. It is artwork, not a broken page.
private: Give a gilded fictional error and invite the recipient to deliver an extravagant acceptance speech.
example: Recognition could not be found. This document has been supplied instead.

name: The Over-Sponsored Button
tagline: An impressive supporting cast. Absolutely no plot.
summary: A button with nothing useful to accomplish.
public: A named patron credit beside an intentionally useless button on its own page. Clicks are never visitor statistics.
private: Dedicate an entirely useless button and invite everyone to announce what it almost achieved.
example: Made possible by someone who had better things to do.

name: The Empty Wing
tagline: A museum extension of impeccable emptiness.
summary: A dedication to an entirely empty gallery.
public: A named dedication inside a fictional empty museum wing. No ownership of physical space.
private: Give an empty-wing dedication, then lead a tour describing the remarkable absence of exhibits.
example: A generous contribution to the preservation of absolutely nothing.

name: The Unnecessary Ribbon
tagline: A grand opening for no particular occasion.
summary: A ceremony in search of an occasion.
public: A named ceremonial opening with your dedication and a replayable opening ceremony.
private: Print a ceremonial opening, then hold a ribbon ceremony using an imaginary ribbon.
example: Today we open the next chapter of something we have not yet identified.

name: The Invisible Monument
tagline: Remarkable from every angle. Especially the ones without it.
summary: An inscription for something you cannot see.
public: A named inscription for a fictional invisible monument. No land, monument or legal title is sold.
private: Give an inscription, then ask the recipient to describe the monument in impossible detail.
example: For the quiet contributions that nobody saw, but everyone appreciated.
